question.text: Grameen Urja Pvt Ltd, an FPE (Section 8 Company) supplying off-grid solar lamps to tribal villages in Jharkhand, has 3-year average revenue of Rs. 12 crore. Mr. Arjun Desai, SIA, must verify that at least 67% is derived from the target population. What is the MINIMUM revenue (any of the three tests) that must flow from eligible activities to the target population?

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 3.1.1(c) of Chapter 3 states that a Social Enterprise shall have at least 67% of its activities qualifying as eligible activities to the target population. This can be ascertained via Revenue, Expenditure, or Customer-base — any ONE limb. 67% of Rs. 12 crore = Rs. 8.04 crore. The SIA must confirm one limb crosses 67% and document the chosen limb in the assessment note. The Trap: 50% is a common NPO-finance threshold (e.g., Section 10(23C) thresholds historically), but not the SSE test. 85% is the Section 11 application threshold under the Income Tax Act. 100% is unrealistic. Candidates must not confuse tax-law 85% with SEBI's 67% SSE threshold. Cross-Exam Context: X-A / X-B (IA L1/L2) reference 85% application of trust income under Section 11. XV (Research Analyst) and XII (SMF) do not test 67%. V-A (MF Distributor) covers 80G (50%/100% deduction) — don't swap. Assessor's Pro-Tip: When choosing between the three limbs for your attestation, pick the one with the STRONGEST documentary support — usually Expenditure (traceable to vouchers and bank statements) over Customer-base (requires KYC-style beneficiary proof). Document your limb choice in the engagement letter and in the SIA report — it anchors the sampling plan.
